frame.goal: Find out who rings the drowned bell and stop the Hollow Choir before it rises.
frame.stakes: Fail: the drowned congregation walks into Gullwick. Win: Teo learns where Mira went.
frame.pressure: The bell rings every second night and the humming grows louder.
frame.finale: Under the bay, in the drowned chapel.
frame.moves_main_plot: Shows that the Archive hid what the bell is.
frame.pulls_in: Teo's sister Mira; Vessa's harbor debt.

scenes.title: Arrival in Gullwick
scenes.summary: The party lands; Maren Vosk warns them off and mentions the Pellow boys.

scenes.title: The bell at midnight
scenes.summary: The drowned bell rings twelve times; a choir hums; Teo says Mira heard it too.

transcript.text:
# Session 1 – transcript

Invented example data for a prototype. 0:12:10.

---

**GM** _[0:00:04]_
You land at Gullwick at dusk. Fog, tar, gulls. The piers at the far end are rotting.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:00:12]_
I'm Teo, I used to run letters for the Archive. I'm here looking for my sister.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:00:20]_
Vessa keeps her hood up. She owes the harbor money and doesn't want to be recognized.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:00:27]_
Oren, hedge-priest, I just follow these two around and patch them up.

**GM** _[0:00:40]_
A woman stomps down the pier toward you, chewing something. Cloves, by the smell.

**Speaker 1** _[0:00:48]_
You lot don't want to be here after the bell. Last time that bell rang, the Pellow boys walked into the sea and never came out.

**GM** _[0:01:02]_
That's Maren Vosk, the harbor-master. She never finishes a sentence if she can spit a clove instead.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:01:10]_
What bell?

**Speaker 1** _[0:01:13]_
The one that sank with the chapel. Go home.

**GM** _[0:06:30]_
At midnight, from under the bay, a bell rings. Twelve times. Something hums along with it, low, like a choir.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:06:45]_
Mira heard that bell too. The night she left. She wrote about it.

scenes.title: The ferry
scenes.summary: Old Hesk ferries the party; he goes overboard and seems dead.

scenes.title: The Archive annex
scenes.summary: A mural shows the Pale Abbot with the bell rope; the archivist points them to Saltmere Mine.

transcript.text:
# Session 2 – transcript

Invented example data for a prototype. 0:10:30.

---

**GM** _[0:00:05]_
Next morning you take the ferry across the estuary to the Archive annex. The ferryman is Old Hesk, ninety if he's a day.

**Speaker 1** _[0:00:14]_
Hold the rail. River's angry since the bell.

**GM** _[0:00:20]_
Hesk hums sea shanties out of tune and calls everyone "lamb".

**GM** _[0:02:40]_
Halfway across, a wave slaps the ferry and Hesk goes over the side. Oren, you pull him out, but he's not moving.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:02:55]_
Is he dead?

**GM** _[0:02:58]_
He's grey and cold and not breathing that you can tell. You leave him with the ferry-house keeper and go on.

**GM** _[0:05:10]_
In the Archive annex there's a mural of the old chapel: monks in white, and above them a pale abbot holding a bell rope, his eyes painted over.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:05:25]_
Who's the abbot?

**GM** _[0:05:28]_
No name. The archivist just calls him the Pale Abbot and says nobody knows.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:08:40]_
We should look at Saltmere Mine sometime, the archivist said the chapel's bell metal came from there.

**GM** _[0:08:50]_
The archivist nods. Saltmere, up the cliff path, closed for forty years.

scenes.title: A boat at pier four
scenes.summary: Sela Thorn, a tide-reader, agrees to row the party to the chapel by day only; she says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang.

scenes.title: Saltmere Mine
scenes.summary: Warm flooded tunnel with floating hymn-book pages; one has "M. Brand" in Mira's hand. Vessa and Oren suspect Maren.

scenes.title: The shore at midnight
scenes.summary: Fishermen warn of the Kelp Mother; the bell rings, the humming is louder, pale shapes stand in rows under the water.

scenes.title: The Tarred Gull
scenes.summary: Bram the innkeeper serves stew; the party plans to dive to the chapel at low tide at first light.

transcript.text:
# Session 3 – transcript

Invented example data for a prototype. 0:25:40 · speakers as labeled by the transcription service.

| Speaker | Talk time |
|---|---:|
| GM | 9 min |
| Speaker 1 | 5 min |
| Jonas (Teo) | 4 min |
| Dana (Vessa) | 4 min |
| Priya (Oren) | 3 min |

---

**GM** _[0:00:05]_
Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:00:14]_
Anyone around who could row us out past the breakwater?

**GM** _[0:00:19]_
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

**Speaker 1** _[0:00:27]_
You want the old chapel. Everyone who comes here wants the old chapel.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:00:33]_
And who are you?

**Speaker 1** _[0:00:36]_
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.

**GM** _[0:00:42]_
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:00:51]_
Can I roll persuasion to get a better price?

**GM** _[0:00:54]_
Sure, go.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:00:57]_
Fourteen.

**GM** _[0:01:00]_
Fine, she'll do it for two silver.

**Speaker 1** _[0:01:06]_
Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:01:12]_
Did she just call herself Sella?

**GM** _[0:01:14]_
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:01:20]_
Ask her about the mine. Somebody said the Saltmere Mine closed.

**Speaker 1** _[0:01:26]_
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:01:35]_
Warm water in a salt mine. That's not creepy at all.

**GM** _[0:01:39]_
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

**GM** _[0:05:48]_
Okay, you decide to look at the mine first since it's on the way. You walk up the cliff path for about an hour.

**GM** _[0:06:02]_
The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:06:20]_
I light a lantern and go in first.

**GM** _[0:06:24]_
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:06:40]_
I fish one out. What's on it?

**GM** _[0:06:44]_
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:06:55]_
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:07:03]_
Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:07:12]_
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

**GM** _[0:07:15]_
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:07:20]_
Nine.

**GM** _[0:07:23]_
You don't find anything else. Oren, take two damage from the bad air.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:07:28]_
Ouch. Okay, down to eleven.

**GM** _[0:13:40]_
You get back to Gullwick by dusk, and you decide to go down to the shore below the old chapel ruins anyway, Sela's warning or not.

**GM** _[0:14:02]_
The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:14:15]_
Are there people around?

**GM** _[0:14:18]_
Two fishermen hauling their boat up. One of them sees you looking at the water.

**Speaker 1** _[0:14:24]_
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:14:33]_
The Kelp Mother. Great. Is that real?

**GM** _[0:14:36]_
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

**GM** _[0:15:10]_
And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.

**GM** _[0:15:24]_
(to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:15:30]_
Do we see anything in the water?

**GM** _[0:15:33]_
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:15:45]_
Nope. Nope nope nope. We're leaving.

**GM** _[0:19:50]_
You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:20:05]_
Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.

**Priya (Oren)** _[0:20:14]_
At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:20:20]_
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:20:31]_
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

**GM** _[0:20:35]_
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

**Speaker 1** _[0:20:41]_
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.

**GM** _[0:20:48]_
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.

**Dana (Vessa)** _[0:20:58]_
Bram, do you know the harbor-master well?

**Speaker 1** _[0:21:02]_
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

**Jonas (Teo)** _[0:21:12]_
Long rest at the inn?

**GM** _[0:21:15]_
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.
